evaluations.method: For each of the report's universe questions and each mode, recall@K (K from the report: 1, 5, 10, 30) = labelled targets ranked at or above K divided by the question's labelled targets, and reciprocal rank = 1 / best labelled rank (0 if none), recomputed from the report's targetRanks; means over the questions; retrieved IDs outside the labels are unjudged (precision@K not measurable; nDCG not computed: no graded labels); checks compare the recomputation with the report's own numbers and the benchmark sha256.
evaluations.variability: percentile bootstrap over questions (paired across modes and metrics), seed 20261122, 2000 resamples, nearest-rank 2.5 % and 97.5 %; every table headed EXPLORATORY (n = 11) and never read as generalization
evaluations.knownGap: benchmark-v1's labels were generated from the Phase 7 graph's own rankings (graph-only agrees partly by construction) and from a different graph run than the deployed Phase 14 graph (3r R2); 19 questions are not comparable and excluded from every mode by design; no OpenSearch tier

Every rate has numerator, denominator, inclusion rule and kind; claim-type rows are not measurable wherever the frozen fields hold no type; each source carries its code version, prompt set and graph run with the origin of each label (file, argument or not available).
evaluations.evidenceKind: a (verifier-reported claim statuses, abstention codes, answer key and verifier tests: internal consistency, never accuracy); the optional dblp.org existence check is b and is recorded on the rating sheet (E11)
evaluations.variability: intervals only over independent answers (human decision on P16-C-02, decision 13 item 9): answers count as independent only when there are at least 2 of them and each answers a distinct question; claim rates: percentile bootstrap over answers (ratio of sums, seed 20261122, 2000 resamples) only where per-answer counts exist, the answers are independent and at least 2 of them have claims in the rate's set (the answers that carry its denominator; with exactly 1 the set is descriptive, note 'descriptive; 1 answer(s) with claims in this set, ...'; with 0 its rows are not measurable), 'no dependence-aware interval' for attempt-06's aggregated counts; answer-level rates (abstention): Wilson score 95% only over independent answers (attempt-06's benchmark questions, one answer each; a denominator of 1 gets no interval); every other rate is descriptive (k, n, proportion, empty ci_low and ci_high, ci_method 'no interval (descriptive)', a note starting 'descriptive;'): the D-query explain rows always ('explain rows are neither independent nor a random sample'), clip 01's audit after its attempts are collapsed (one answer, so no interval), and demo answers that repeat a question; nothing pooled across sources or code versions
evaluations.knownGap: independent factual accuracy of answers is not independently measurable except the optional dblp.org existence check; attempt-06 holds aggregated counts only (rag-runtime/2, prompts v2, Phase 7 export via the benchmark harness, fake embeddings); load-explain.csv holds no verification counts or codes, and FECD-3 applies to its rows (explain shows the latest execution only); clip 01 holds counts but no claim texts; no claim type is stored per claim except through cited evidence types in the demo answers; prompt set labels for D-query and clip 01 code version are not recorded in the frozen files and are reported not available

evaluations.evidenceKind: a (the project's own records), audited by c (the human's 20-event spot check: classification agreement, not completeness)
evaluations.variability: counts with denominators; no interval (the records are a full population, not a random sample); the audit's agreement rate is reported
evaluations.knownGap: report formats changed over the phases; findings outside markdown tables, prose step logs (phase 11) and per-agent first-pass attribution at phase granularity are limits of the rules; the audit measures classification agreement, not extraction completeness
